details:
Project Details – FIREINTEL

FIREINTEL is a satellite-based wildfire intelligence platform that transforms raw satellite fire observations into accessible geospatial insights. It harmonises active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS, using MODIS and VIIRS satellite datasets, into a unified data framework.

How it works:
The platform processes satellite observations and presents them through an interactive wildfire map, seasonal activity analytics, a burning activity calendar, 3D terrain visualisation, and a geospatial workspace. Users can explore fire activity across geographical regions, compare seasonal patterns, inspect individual satellite observations, and export structured datasets for further research. Copernicus DEM GLO-30 provides additional terrain context.

Benefits and intended impact:
FIREINTEL simplifies the analysis of fragmented satellite datasets and helps researchers and environmental analysts understand the spatial and seasonal distribution of fire activity. Its intended impact is to support environmental research, improve access to satellite-derived information, and enable more informed wildfire monitoring and decision-making.

Technology used:

  • Frontend: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • 3D Visualisation & Animations: Three.js, Framer Motion, GSAP
  • Backend & Data Processing: Python, FastAPI, DuckDB
  • Geospatial Data: NASA FIRMS MODIS/VIIRS, Copernicus DEM GLO-30
  • Infrastructure & Deployment: AWS, Docker, Nginx

Factors considered:
Our team prioritised data accuracy, sensor differences, geographical boundaries, missing timestamps, performance, scalability, usability, and scientific transparency. We distinguish satellite fire detections from confirmed fire incidents and avoid presenting unvalidated predictions as facts.

Our vision is to make satellite-derived wildfire intelligence more accessible, understandable, and useful for environmental protection.
